newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 22.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 22.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
** India's largest private firm Reliance Industries will announce results for the financial year ended March 31, 1997 on Tuesday.
A Reuters poll of 28 securities firms on Monday showed Reliance would post a net profit of 12.06 billion rupees for 1996/97, recording a 7.63 percent fall over the same period a year ago.
** India's new prime minister, Inder Kumar Gujral, prepares to face a vote of confidence on Tuesday at the head of a centre-left coalition that changed its leader to win back a former ally.
The 15-party alliance under Gujral was expected to prove easily that it commands a parliamentary majority after patching things up with the Congress party.
Parliament was scheduled to convene at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT) to debate India's third government in 11 months, formed to avoid mid-term elections. Voting was expected at the end of the day.

** In his maiden speech after being sworn in as the prime minister, Gujral told a business meeting that the nation could continue to achieve seven percent annual growth of gross domestic product (GDP), which was the average rate over the past three years.

Gujral assured the business leaders that his centre-left government would maintain continuity in economic policies. "I commit here that economic policy continuity will be firmly assured by my government," he said.
** Weak demand and rising costs will squeeze profit growth of top Indian firms in 1996/97 (April-March) with some sectors like cement and steel showing lower earnings, a Reuter poll showed on Monday.

Analysts' earnings forecasts for 28 firms on benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) top-30 index showed average net profit growth falling sharply to 5.9 percent from about 25 percent in 1995/96 and 32 percent in 1994/95.
